integrator_questions: With mass at 1.2 kg, does the controller need more kp to hold the bend response, or less kd to stop the signal lagging? Compare the gain margin with the 1.0 kg run.
Where does max_error occur now: on the oval's tightest bend or on the s-bend and slalom? If it is still at bend entry, the peak is lag-limited and mass alone will not close the gap.
Does steering_oscillation or control_effort rise with the heavier robot, and does line_loss_events change on the slalom?

intent: Single-variable mass test on the best design (iteration 7, 73.33). Mass goes from 1.0 kg to 1.2 kg. Everything else stays at the iteration 7 values: 80 mm sensor row, 12 mm sensors on a 12 mm pitch, 0.12 m track, 0.03 m wheels, 0.12 m body width and 0.18 m body length. Expected: max_error at or near 0.060 m, oval progress at or above 0.227, and a score above 73.33.
learning: Track is at its best value (0.12 m), lookahead is at its maximum (0.08 m), and mass rises monotonically with diminishing returns (0.6 kg 55.4, 0.8 kg 69.2, 1.0 kg 73.3). If 1.2 kg beats 1.0 kg, the optimum lies above 1.0 kg and the next test is wheel_radius. If 1.2 kg falls back, 1.0 kg is near the local optimum and wheel_radius is the next test, with sensor pitch after that.
rationale: Scores by iteration on the same base: 60 mm row 65.96; 40 mm row 52.25; 80 mm row 69.18; 80 mm with 0.10 m track 53.14; 80 mm with 0.14 m track 60.26; 80 mm with 0.6 kg 55.45; 80 mm with 1.0 kg 73.33 (best). Lookahead is monotone and now sits at the 0.08 m contract maximum. Track peaks at 0.12 m. Mass is monotone too: 0.6 kg gave 55.4, 0.8 kg gave 69.2 and 1.0 kg gave 73.3. The gain is shrinking (+14 then +4), so the optimum is probably somewhere above 1.0 kg. Max error stays at 0.060 to 0.066 m on every track in every run, just over the off-track limit, while RMS error is 0.02 to 0.03 m. The failure is a transient bend peak, not a steady offset, and body width cannot move the limit. I will keep the 1.0 kg design and change one variable, mass, to 1.2 kg. If the score rises, the trend continues with diminishing returns. If it falls, 1.0 kg is near the local optimum and the next single-variable test is wheel_radius. Expected result: max error near or below 0.060 m, oval and slalom progress at or above the 1.0 kg values, and a score of about 74 to 76. Risk: rolling and slip losses at higher mass could reduce progress on the oval.
